title: Combination product present but authors attribute event to one ingredient only

facts.statement: A combination medicinal product contains Ingredient A and Ingredient B.
The adverse event occurs while the combination product is used.
The authors explicitly attribute the event to Ingredient A.
The source does not support Ingredient B as causal.

rationale: Each ingredient must be assessed independently.
Author attribution and supporting evidence outweigh simple co-occurrence.
Combination membership does not transfer causality to every ingredient.
prohibitedConclusions: Classify both ingredients as suspect solely because both are present in the administered combination.

regulatoryReferences: GVP Module VI: literature/multiple medicinal-product causality principles
